verdict.rationale: LiteLLM's proxy/router documents availability-driven policy routing. It retries, then falls back to another model group, so a failing model fails over to a healthy backup. It also offers content-policy fallbacks, load-balancing across deployments, and cooldowns and timeouts. Cost- or capability-based routing rules are only implied by a marketing line about sending each request to 'the model that should handle it'. Missing for 10: documented cost-based routing rules, documented capability-based routing rules, and independent hands-on corroboration of mid-task switching.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can switch models mid-task by policy — cost, capability, or availability — through gateway routing rules

citations.quote: If a call fails after num_retries, LiteLLM falls back to another model group, so a failing model or provider automatically fails over to a healthy backup.
litellm proxy will loop through all the model_groups specified in `fallbacks=["gpt-3.5-turbo"]`
Basic reliability logic - cooldowns, fallbacks, timeouts and retries (fixed + exponential backoff) across multiple deployments/providers.
content_policy_fallbacks: For litellm.ContentPolicyViolationError - LiteLLM maps content policy violation errors across providers
